record.paper_title: A New Paradigm for Scattering Theory of Linear and Nonlinear Waves: Review and Open Problems
record.original_question: For other evolution systems such as Boltzmann-type equations, including singular realistic kernels, or dispersive and fluid-type equations in Fourier space, what hypotheses on asymptotic solutions and what definitions of channel wave operators make scattering-theoretic large-time analysis possible?

evidence.quote: 14.6. Other Classes of Equations. Many other systems may exhibit large-time behavior amenable to scattering theory methods. However, in these cases, one needs a working hypothesis about the form of asymptotic solutions, and an idea of how to introduce appropriate channel wave operators. As demonstrated in the section on self-similar solutions, the corresponding ”asymptotic dynamics” may involve a simple scaling transformation with ”time” represented by α lnt. Interesting cases include Boltzmann-type equations, with or without singular (i.e., realistic) Kernels. Other notable examples involve dispersive equations in the Fourier space of the equation, as encountered in fluid dynamics.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Develop a scattering theory for evolution equations beyond the classical dispersive setting. Concretely, consider the following two families of evolution problems:

(a) Boltzmann-type kinetic equations of the form
   ∂_t f + v·∇_x f = Q(f,f),
where f = f(t,x,v) ≥ 0, (x,v) ∈ ℝ^d × ℝ^d, and Q is a bilinear collision operator
   Q(f,f)(v) = ∫_{ℝ^d}∫_{S^{d-1}} B(v−v_*, σ)[f(v')f(v_*') − f(v)f(v_*)] dσ dv_*,
with v' = (v+v_*)/2 + |v−v_*|σ/2, v_*' = (v+v_*)/2 − |v−v_*|σ/2, allowing physically realistic (singular, non-cutoff) collision kernels B.

(b) Dispersive or fluid-type equations analyzed in Fourier space, i.e., evolution PDEs whose solutions û(t,ξ) satisfy a transport/oscillatory equation in the frequency variable ξ.

For these systems, the large-time dynamics may not be free-evolution-like but may instead involve a self-similar "asymptotic dynamics" implemented by a scaling transformation with rescaled time τ = α log t for some α > 0.

The problem is to:
1. Formulate a precise working hypothesis on the form of admissible asymptotic profiles (e.g. self-similar solutions, modified profiles in Fourier space) describing the large-time behavior of solutions in each setting.
2. Define corresponding channel wave operators Ω_± : data ↦ asymptotic profile (and their inverses, the scattering maps) on appropriate function spaces, possibly incorporating logarithmic-in-time rescaling, modified phases, or other corrections needed to compensate long-range/self-similar effects.
3. Prove existence, uniqueness, and (where appropriate) asymptotic completeness of these channel wave operators, thereby establishing a scattering-theoretic decomposition of the large-time dynamics for Boltzmann equations with singular kernels and for dispersive/fluid-type equations in Fourier space.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a programmatic open problem asking for the right hypotheses and channel wave operator definitions enabling scattering analysis for Boltzmann-type equations (including with singular kernels) and dispersive/fluid-type equations in Fourier space. While partial results exist (e.g., self-similar/eternal solutions for Boltzmann with Mischler–Mouhot and others; modified scattering for NLS/Hartree, KdV, gravity water waves), no unified framework answering the general question has been established, and the question is posed as an open direction.
